description:
Decide which crate hosts each public type the gf2-algebra-permanent epic introduces, ensuring no circular dependencies and a consistent layering across the workspace. ## Background The new `gf2-algebra` crate hosts permanent algorithms and packed small-prime field representations. This issue settles which types live where: - What stays in `gf2-core`: bedrock primitives only (`FiniteField`, `Fp

`, `BitVec`, `BitMatrix`, `Fp

::*`). - What moves into `gf2-algebra`: `PackedField` trait, `Bipedal3`/`Bipedal5`/`Bipedal7` packed types, `permanent_*` algorithms, Gray-code enumerator, parallel and GPU dispatch glue. - What lives in `gf2-kernels-simd`: SIMD bipedal kernels. - What lives in `gf2-kernels-hip`: GPU permanent kernels. Output: a short decision doc ($\le 200$ lines) listing every public type the epic introduces, naming its home crate, and showing the dependency-direction graph. ## Success Criteria - [ ] [hard] Decision doc exists at `dev/plans/d1a_gf2_algebra_boundary.md` and is attached via `jit doc add`. - [ ] [hard] No circular crate dependencies are proposed; `gf2-algebra → gf2-core` is the only mandatory non-feature-gated forward edge into other workspace crates. Feature-gated edges to `gf2-kernels-simd` (default-on `simd` feature) and `gf2-kernels-hip` (default-off `hip` feature) are permitted. (Amended 2026-05-09 per user approval; reviewer's strict reading of the original "only forward edge required" wording conflicted with the architectural reality documented in epic doc §5 / §10 / §11.) - [ ] [hard] The doc enumerates every public type the linked epic design doc mentions and assigns each to exactly one crate. - [ ] [hard] The doc explicitly justifies why bipedal types do not live in `gf2-core` (they pack many $\mathbb{F}_3$ elements per word and are not field elements).
title: Decide gf2-algebra crate boundary against gf2-core
